title: IAM, Secrets & Least Privilege
interviewAnswer: Production services should receive only the permissions they need, with credentials kept in secret-management mechanisms rather than source code or images. Identity and network boundaries are part of ML system design.
why: Security is a system-design expectation: models and data often access sensitive storage, APIs and credentials.
intuition: Least privilege means every user/service gets only the permissions needed, for only as long and narrow a scope as practical. Secrets should be injected securely, not baked into code/images.
deepDive: Use workload identities/roles rather than long-lived static keys where possible. Separate authentication (who are you?) from authorization (what may you do?). Scope object/container/model registry permissions, encrypt data in transit/at rest, rotate secrets and log access. Network controls and private endpoints may reduce exposure. Treat retrieved documents/model outputs as untrusted content, not authorization decisions.
workedExample: An inference container needs read access to one model bucket and write access to one result prefix, not administrator permission to the whole cloud account.
commonMistakes: Putting cloud keys in Git/Docker images.
Granting broad admin roles “temporarily” and never removing them.
Letting an LLM decide whether a user is authorized.
followUps: Why workload roles over static keys?
How would you secure a RAG system?
production: Use centralized secret/identity management, short-lived credentials, audit logs, permission reviews and automated scanning for leaked secrets/dependencies.
